title: An animator with timed frames
description:
Write an animator where every frame has its own duration, and that reports animation events:

```cpp
struct Animation { std::vector<float> durations; bool loop; };   // one duration (seconds) per frame

class Animator
{
public:
    void play(const Animation* a);          // restarts only if a is a different animation
    std::vector<int> update(float dt);      // the frames *entered* during this update, in order
    int frame() const;                      // current frame index, 0-based
    bool finished() const;                  // one-shot animation past its last frame's end
};
```

- After `play`, the current frame is 0, and frame 0 counts as entered by the **next** `update` (so an event on frame 0 fires once).
- `update(dt)` adds `dt` to the time and returns every frame whose **start** time was passed during this update (including frame 0 right after `play`). A looping animation wraps around, so a long `dt` can enter the same frames again: report each entry in order.
- A one-shot animation stays on its last frame. `finished` becomes true when the time reaches the total of all durations; no more frames are entered after that.

Example: durations `{ 0.1, 0.2, 0.1 }` looping, so the frames start at 0, 0.1 and 0.3, and the loop comes back to frame 0 at 0.4. `update(0.05)` → `{0}`; `update(0.1)` → `{1}` (time 0.15); `update(0.2)` → `{2}` (time 0.35); `update(0.1)` → `{0}` (time 0.45).
hints: Keep the current frame and the time spent in it. While that time is at least the frame's duration, subtract the duration and move on to the next frame (or wrap, or finish).
